source.text: እለ፡ በልዑ፡ ኵሎ፡ ጻማ፡ ሰብእ፡ †እስከ፡† ስእኑዎሙ፡ *ሰብእ፡ ሴስዮት።
source.note: Complete Charles 1906 printed page 16 inspected first in a separately photographed Uoft leaf and then cross-checked against a fresh render of pinned PDF page 54. The same printed unit, marked connector, and final feeding form agree; these are not independent manuscript witnesses. Edition daggers and asterisk are retained; raised apparatus callouts are not running source. No alternative source or historical reconstruction adopted.

translation.text: They devoured all the produce of human labor[b], until[a] people were unable to feed them[c].

footnotes.text: “Until” translates the conjunction Charles prints between daggers. In apparatus note 11 he treats the Greek conjunction it represents as corrupt and proposes a different Ethiopic reading. This translation follows the printed body, not that proposal. The daggers mark disputed text, not a gap.

The source begins with “who,” referring to the giants in the preceding verse; “they” lets the English verse stand on its own. “Produce of human labor” takes the labor noun to mean what labor produces, a sense Dillmann gives in column 1272, citing Enoch 7:3. Charles’s apparatus note 10 questions the printed form rendered “all”; the translation retains it.

The printed feeding form is ሴስዮት. Dillmann’s feeding entry (column 393) cites Enoch 7:3, and his Grammar §125 explains the nominal infinitive endings -ōt and -ō. Here the ending belongs to the infinitive, not a plural pronoun. “Them” is expressed by the suffix on the preceding inability verb; Dillmann’s inability entry (column 377) describes that placement for a pronoun referring to the infinitive’s object.
